subject.title: Control UI: media/config endpoints 401 over Tailscale Serve origin, breaking local media previews (works fine via loopback)

question: Should verified Tailscale Serve identity, with whois verification and Control UI browser-origin checks, authorize the Control UI bootstrap, avatar, and assistant-media HTTP read routes without a bearer token?
rationale: This is a deliberate auth-boundary expansion, not only a mechanical bug fix, and it decides whether Tailscale identity crosses from Control UI WebSocket auth into HTTP routes that expose config and local media metadata.

options.title: Approve narrow HTTP read parity
options.body: Accept the linked PR shape after confirming the route scope is limited to Control UI reads and ordinary HTTP APIs remain unchanged.

options.title: Keep HTTP reads token-only
options.body: Reject the tokenless HTTP read carve-out and instead make the UI use an explicit bearer, device token, or another bootstrap recovery path.

options.title: Fold into proxy bootstrap design
options.body: Defer this issue into the broader reverse-proxy Control UI bootstrap work tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12441.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow HTTP read parity
recommendation.body: Accept the linked PR shape after confirming the route scope is limited to Control UI reads and ordinary HTTP APIs remain unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the clearest prior reviewer for the adjacent Control UI auth-boundary discussion and is better positioned than the current candidate PR author to decide the security model.
